title: Supported means the passage says it
statement: Besides checking that a quote is exact, check that the passage itself states everything the claim says, not merely that the claim is plausible, and audit 'partly supported' verdicts.
example: One span labelled fully supported added a fact the paragraph never stated, so only outside knowledge could support it.
detail: A second model re-graded 30 support labels from a training set, stratified 10 per class, and agreed with 70% overall and 60% on 'partly supported', with two of those pulled up to 'fully' and two down to 'no' (`project_self_rag_label_audit_rebuild_trigger.md`). The clearest disagreement was a span labelled fully supported that added a fact the paragraph never stated, so it needed outside knowledge. 'Partly supported' verdicts need an audit of their own.
against: This is one model checked against another on 10 spans per class, so its disagreements are not errors against a person's key, and the re-grader leaned lenient on the 'no' class, moving three labels to 'partly' and none the other way (same file, line 43). The evaluation design is a draft: no model has been run under it (`uae-education-ai/EVALUATION.md`, line 3).

evidence.quote: The partially class is **bidirectionally noisy** — 2 cases pulled UP to "fully" (Quill under-rated), 2 cases pulled DOWN to "no" (Quill over-rated).
- Atlas verdict: "no" — paragraph mentions debate over treatment, NOT conversion to Christianity. Span injects fact requiring outside knowledge.
The "no" class is asymmetrically lenient on Atlas's side (3 pulled "no" → "partially", 0 the other way), consistent with 3.1-pro slightly more accepting of thematic-but-not-literal entailment.
- The quote doesn't mention water, so the model answer asserts something its own evidence doesn't show.

Mechanically verify that each quote is an exact fragment substring. … rate whether the quote actually supports the stated verdict and rule: 0 = absent or misleading, 1 = relevant but incomplete, 2 = sufficient and faithful.
The script doesn't check a write-frame's revealed quote against the revealed answer.
